parts.note: plays on 'the luck of the draw': candyfloss is made by spinning, so its fortune lies in how the sugar was spun

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about what fortune befalls a stick of candyfloss.
explanation.walkthrough: Candyfloss (US cotton candy) is sugar whirled into threads; the clue twists the phrase 'the luck of the draw', since 'spun' can describe a wheel of fortune too.
explanation.definitionFit: Candyfloss is a fairground confection of sugar drawn into fine threads by a whirling drum.

clue.text: Bookseller who maintained turnover with diminishing stock

definitions.text: Bookseller who maintained turnover with diminishing stock

parts.words: Bookseller who maintained turnover with diminishing stock
parts.note: the Cumaean prophetess offered nine books to King Tarquin, burning three each time he refused, but kept the price the same

explanation.surface: A shrewd bookshop owner keeps takings level while stock runs down.
explanation.walkthrough: In Roman legend the prophetess sold the last three of her books to Tarquin for the price first asked for all nine.
explanation.definitionFit: A prophetess of the ancient world, like the one at Cumae who sold Rome its prophetic books.

parts.note: an usher was an assistant schoolmaster
Ed is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster named Edward is introduced.
explanation.definitionFit: To be shown in or presented to people, as an attendant guides a guest.

clue.text: Not all are like this to me

parts.note: so means in this way or like this
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone thinks not everyone feels as they do.
explanation.definitionFit: A part rather than the whole, a portion of a group.

clue.text: Some of Wales' is Mac beth's

parts.note: Glam. is the short form of Glamorgan, a county making up part of Wales

explanation.surface: A fragment of Welsh land belongs to a Scottish character.
explanation.walkthrough: Glamorgan is a county of south Wales; the clue splits Macbeth as Mac-beth across a line, and his title was Thane of the castle named.
explanation.definitionFit: Macbeth was Thane of this Scottish castle and place in Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: Dear cell, unkempt but not forgotten

indicators.note: unkempt means untidy or dishevelled, so the letters of the two words are messed up

explanation.surface: A fond memory of an untidy room.
explanation.definitionFit: Brought back to mind and remembered rather than lost from memory.

parts.note: reads like a jet-setting cardiologist, but the winged boy of myth deals in hearts with his arrows

explanation.surface: A cardiologist who travels by plane between patients.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman god of love is shown winged, shooting arrows into lovers' hearts.

clue.text: Cuts of liquidity including a different coin: are religiously assumed

definitions.note: an adjective phrase standing for garments put on by clergy

indicators.note: including means one piece takes another inside it

parts.note: canals are cuts filled with water

indicators.note: a different coin means the four letters arranged another way

explanation.surface: Coins cut and mixed into a reserve are taken on faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' and 'are' only link; 'assumed' means put on, as clothes are, so the vestments are what is religiously assumed.
explanation.definitionFit: Clerical vestments prescribed by church law are put on by clergy for services.

clue.text: That's more, than one feather in one's cap

definitions.text: That's more, than one feather in one's cap

parts.words: That's more, than one feather in one's cap
parts.note: an achievement is a feather in one's cap, but here a whole plume of feathers on a helmet is meant

explanation.surface: Praising a person with many achievements to their credit.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally a tuft of plumes on a helmet, it now means stylish flair.

clue.text: Country that is not a party to the Convention

definitions.meaning: a historic central European kingdom, now part of the Czech Republic

definitions.text: that is not a party to the Convention
definitions.meaning: the land figuratively inhabited by unconventional artists and free spirits

explanation.definitionFit: A former kingdom in central Europe, and the name for the world of artists who ignore social convention.

clue.text: They evoke tender feelings in the seats of learning

definitions.text: They evoke tender feelings in the seats of learning

parts.words: They evoke tender feelings in the seats of learning
parts.note: sounds like affection at universities, but 'tender' means sore and 'seats' are the backsides of schoolboys being beaten

explanation.surface: Fond emotions stirred up at the great universities.
explanation.definitionFit: Beatings with a cane, once a school punishment, leave the sufferer's bottom sore.

parts.note: an enticement, with 'misrule' hinting that the word rule, set out wrongly, gives the letters

explanation.surface: Why anarchy appeals to people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misrule' read as 'rule, mis-set' points to rearranging RULE, though no separate word signals it, so the clue works as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: An attraction or enticement draws someone in, as bait does a fish.

clue.text: Say love, here's Willie with his "Ayrshire"

parts.note: Willie and Bill are both pet forms of William
with means and, joining two things
an Ayrshire is a Scottish breed of cattle, and coo is the Scots word for cow

explanation.surface: A Scot named Willie and his favourite cow being described fondly.
explanation.walkthrough: An Ayrshire is a breed of dairy cow from south-west Scotland, so Willie, as a Scot, would call it his 'coo'; 'here's' and 'his' only join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To bill and coo is to murmur endearments like courting doves, so to whisper love.

parts.note: nous is good sense or brains, so its offspring is an idea born of the mind

explanation.definitionFit: An original idea or invention springing from one person's mind.

parts.note: Victorien Sardou wrote the 1882 play whose heroine's name was given to a soft felt hat

explanation.surface: Headgear belonging to a French dramatist.
explanation.walkthrough: Sardou's play, in which Sarah Bernhardt wore such a hat, gave the hat its name.
explanation.definitionFit: The soft brimmed felt hat with a creased crown took its name from a play title.

parts.note: a brilliant person is said to set the Thames on fire, putting fire into the water

explanation.surface: A drink invented by a bright young Londoner.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'set the Thames on fire' is a British idiom for doing something remarkable; the Thames is London's river.
explanation.definitionFit: Strong spirits, a term from North American frontier trading for hard liquor.

parts.note: breathing in seaside air fills one's chest with sea, and a sailor's trunk is called after both

explanation.surface: A question about whether luggage breathes in seaside air.
explanation.walkthrough: Ozone was once the popular name for bracing seaside air, so a chest inhaling it is a 'sea chest', the trunk a sailor keeps his kit in.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailor's storage box for belongings carried aboard ship.

clue.text: Is he acting so strangely from divine ignorance?

definitions.text: Is he acting so strangely from divine ignorance?

indicators.note: strangely means oddly, so the letters of the two words are rearranged oddly

explanation.surface: Asking whether a man behaves oddly because he knows nothing of God.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' rearranges ACTING SO, and the whole clue describes one who professes no knowledge of God.
explanation.definitionFit: One who holds that whether God exists cannot be known.

parts.note: a red rag provokes a bull

explanation.surface: Birds that annoy another kind of bird.
explanation.walkthrough: The idea is that red enrages a bull, so a bull-finch would be goaded by birds showing red flanks under their wings, as these thrushes do.
explanation.definitionFit: These are small thrushes with rusty-red flanks under the wing, winter visitors to Britain.

parts.note: Dandie is a Scots pet form of Andrew, and Scott's farmer Dandie bore this surname

explanation.surface: A man called Andrew dressed up as a dandy.
explanation.walkthrough: In Scott's novel Guy Mannering the farmer Andrew, known as Dandie, gave his name to a breed of terrier.
explanation.definitionFit: Surname of Scott's Border farmer Dandie, also a terrier breed named after him.

parts.note: shells fired at sea come from naval guns, and Jane's is the reference book of fighting ships

explanation.surface: Asking a girl named Jane where seashells come from.
explanation.walkthrough: Jane's Fighting Ships is the standard annual directory of the world's navies, so 'Jane' points to naval vessels.
explanation.definitionFit: A naval fighting vessel armed with guns.

definitions.meaning: William ... was Archbishop of Canterbury, Primate of All England
the side of the forehead shows when a head is viewed from the side

explanation.definitionFit: Surname of an Archbishop of Canterbury, and the flat side of the head beside the brow.

parts.note: a drink is wine and a clink, slang for prison, is a cooler, so the phrase reads as a prison for drink

explanation.definitionFit: An ice bucket or chilled vessel keeps bottles cold before serving.

clue.text: Fish in the crop of a bird?

definitions.text: Fish in the crop of a bird?

parts.words: Fish in the crop of a bird?
parts.note: the crop of a bird is its ..., and adding fish gives ..., so this word sits in front of 'fish'

explanation.surface: A bird has swallowed a fish, now stored in its throat pouch.
explanation.definitionFit: The crop, a pouch in a bird's gullet, is also called its craw, as in crawfish.

definitions.meaning: a stretch of barren, empty land

explanation.definitionFit: Barren wilderness land, and the squandering of money by prodigals.

parts.note: in Much Ado About Nothing Beatrice says that at her birth a heavenly body danced, and under that she was born

explanation.surface: A ballerina present at a woman's birth.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's Beatrice says: 'there was a star danced, and under that was I born.'
explanation.definitionFit: A heavenly body seen dancing in the sky when Beatrice was born.

clue.text: Too much is it for the figurative one?

definitions.text: Too much is it for the figurative one?

parts.words: Too much is it for the figurative one?
parts.note: French trop means too much, and one who deals in tropes, figures of speech, fits 'figurative one'

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone given to flowery speech overdoes it.
explanation.walkthrough: TROP is French for 'too much', and the suffix -IST makes a practitioner, so the clue points both ways at a user of tropes.
explanation.definitionFit: A trope is a figure of speech, so a person given to them speaks figuratively.

definitions.meaning: ... as a verb means hurls or tosses
... as a noun are the strips of ground set aside for cricket matches

explanation.definitionFit: To hurl a ball, and the prepared grassy strips used for playing the bat-and-ball game.

clue.text: Carpeted for half that in red

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the letters of the colour word
half picks the back two of the four letters of that

explanation.surface: A rug is laid in place of half of a red one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carpeted' in the sense of being summoned before the boss and scolded, not having a floor covered; 'for' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: To be carpeted is to be called in and scolded, the same as being reprimanded or told off.

definitions.meaning: a fruit tart is a dish served at table
a garden plant, the heliotrope, has the popular name of a fruit tart because of its scent

explanation.definitionFit: A baked fruit pudding, and the country name for the sweet-scented garden heliotrope.
